profile.campus: Sandston, Henrico County, Virginia (QTS Richmond 2 / RIC2 campus)
profile.reading:
RIC2 is QTS's second Richmond area campus, one of three campuses, RIC1, RIC2, and RIC3, that QTS Realty Trust operates within the White Oak Technology Park in Sandston, an unincorporated community in eastern Henrico County east of Richmond. RIC2 sits immediately adjacent to QTS's older RIC1 campus along the same Technology Boulevard corridor. Where RIC1's buildings carry the shared address of 6000 Technology Blvd for DC1 through DC3, with DC4 through DC6 addressed separately on nearby Portugee Road, RIC2's five buildings run in a contiguous block further down the same road, addressed 6030, 6040, 6050, 6060, and 6070 Technology Boulevard, Sandston, Virginia 23150. QTS's own numbering skips DC4 within RIC2, this registry located only DC1, DC2, DC3, DC5, and DC6 for the campus, and no separately mapped RIC2 DC4 exists in the public record reviewed for this project.

Per QTS's own site, the RIC2 campus is master planned across roughly 85 acres and is designed for 180 megawatts of power capacity once fully built out, a campus wide figure that spans all five buildings rather than a number broken out per building. That makes RIC2 meaningfully smaller in land area than RIC1's 207 acre, 238 megawatt, six building campus, but RIC2 is the newer of the two. A QTS blog post on its own site describes RIC2 DC1 and DC2 specifically as two story buildings, each carrying 36 megawatts of IT capacity, for 72 megawatts combined between the two buildings, with construction documented from February through November 2022 and a targeted completion of 2023 for DC1 and the fourth quarter of 2023 for DC2, the latter also noted in that QTS post as having received an air permit during its construction phase. No comparable building specific power figure was found in this research for DC3, DC5, or DC6, so those three buildings carry no it_capacity_mw, utility_power_mw, standby_generation_mw, or onsite_generation_mw entries here, only the shared campus figure.

This building history places RIC2 as an already established campus, built mostly in the 2022 to 2023 period, and not part of QTS's newer, much larger 2024 era expansion. That later expansion, reported by Richmond BizSense and DataCenterDynamics, involves separate tracts under the RIC4 and RIC5 project names, a 478 acre RIC4 site across Technology Boulevard from the three existing RIC1, RIC2, and RIC3 campuses, and a 622 acre RIC5 site southeast of the I-64 and I-295 interchange along Williamsburg Road, together planned for up to 17 more buildings. RIC2 is not part of either of those newer tracts. DataCenterDynamics's 2026 coverage of that expansion describes RIC1, RIC2, and RIC3 collectively as QTS's three existing Richmond campuses, together already totaling more than 3 million square feet across a dozen operating or under construction buildings, with QTS's overall White Oak vision eventually reaching 26 buildings and roughly 8 million square feet once RIC4 and RIC5 are built out.

Henrico County's broader 2024 planning staff analysis, already documented in this registry's RIC1 research, counts 37 data centers across the full White Oak Technology Park from multiple operators including QTS and Meta, and frames county interest in updated development standards around that cumulative growth rather than around any single building or campus. No rezoning case, board of supervisors minutes, assessor parcel record, or building permit specific to RIC2 individually, as distinct from the county's general White Oak coverage and its 2024 expansion related actions, was located in this research session. QTS Realty Trust, the operator on record for RIC2, is owned by Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust and affiliated Blackstone funds following a roughly 10 billion dollar take private transaction completed August 31, 2021.

RIC2 DC1, at 6030 Technology Boulevard, is one of the two RIC2 buildings QTS has described with any specificity in its own materials, a two story structure with 36 megawatts of IT capacity that QTS targeted for completion in 2023, construction on the building documented by QTS from February through November 2022. Beyond that IT capacity figure and the 2023 completion target, no Henrico County permit, assessor parcel record, Uptime Institute tier certificate, or generation specific figure for this building was located in this research, so its utility power, standby generation, and onsite generation numbers remain unpublished in the sources reviewed and are not asserted here.

reading.body:
RIC2 DC1 is one of two buildings at QTS's Richmond 2 campus in Sandston, Henrico County, for which QTS has published specific power figures. The building is a two-story structure with 36 megawatts of IT capacity, constructed between February and November 2022 and targeted for completion in 2023. Assuming a typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, 36 megawatts of IT load translates to approximately 900 racks. The full RIC2 campus spans five buildings across 85 acres and is planned for 180 megawatts total, though building-specific capacity is published only for DC1 and its sister building DC2, also at 36 megawatts each.

RIC2 DC1 ranks 26th among Virginia facilities with published power capacity and represents roughly 2 percent of the state's published 1,603 megawatts. Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, but only 25 publish power figures, placing RIC2 DC1 in a small set of publicly specified sites. The campus is one of three existing QTS facilities at White Oak Technology Park and is distinct from the operator's separate RIC4 and RIC5 expansion tracts announced in 2024, which together plan 17 additional buildings.

No Henrico County permit record, Uptime Institute certification, utility power figure, standby generation capacity, or onsite generation specification for RIC2 DC1 was located in the published sources reviewed. QTS's own site and blog post provide only the IT capacity and construction timeline. The building's actual utility power draw and backup generation systems remain unpublished.
